doc.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Joe Romano and Buddy Rich wit
summary: Joe Romano's jokes, trading barbs with Buddy Rich and Jimmy Mosher.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Oh, the wise guys. The upstate upstarts, yeah. There was Menza, Romano — he was the biggest wise guy of them all — then Larry Covelli, Sal, Sammy Noto. They were real — Sal Nestico, Joe Romano, boy he’s a real wise guy. He worked with Gap Mangione, Chuck’s older brother you know, playing the piano and Gap, playing the piano. Joe takes a handkerchief and he throws it right across the keyboard like this. “What the hell is that for?” “Illegal use of the hands.” A real wise guy. “Watch out man, I used to be a fighter you know.” He says, “Well take the boxing gloves off when you’re working with me, huh?” No use trying to top Joe. Might as well keep your mouth shut and let him — he used to do that to Buddy Rich, of all people. And Buddy Rich would come right back at him, and those two guys were funny when they’d get in the trailer or in the back rooms. You’d listen to those guys go at it, they were funny man. Oh, they were funny. He loved
him. Buddy Rich loved Joe Romano. Anybody that was a real quick wit he loved. But Joe could blow you know, Joe’s a hell of a player.
You just can’t be funny, you’ve got to play too. Like Buddy could play like a demon. But he was a very funny guy. Jesus, he was a great guy, great.
That’s interesting. I didn’t know anybody had the nerve to try to top Buddy Rich.

Oh yeah. A guy named Jimmy Mosher was with him too. And Buddy’d get so mad he’d throw the sticks at him. But Jimmy always had a funny line, a funny comeback, and nothing he could do you know. They were funny guys man.
